activity.title: "That's not even close to what they said." - anyone who's ever watched the subtitled version of a show or movie where they know the original language And you know what? They're probably right. But there's a good reason 💡 When subtitlers are translating subtitles, they have to think about not only what was said in the original language, but how best to convey that in the space of: 😬 maximum 2 lines 😬 maximum 40 characters per line (with spaces) 😬 between 1 second and 6 seconds 😬 maximum 20 characters per second reading speed 😬 breaking the lines at a logical spot to aid reading 😬 all while making it understandable in another language So yeah, sometimes the subtitle might not be the direct translation of what the character is saying. But does it get the gist of it? Sometimes, that's all we can do. 🤷🏻‍♀️ (📌 limits above are for English subs, other languages vary!) ...more ...more

👀 I heard once that human translation is not a luxury. Because luxury is something we can do without. And no one needs a luxury. I couldn't agree more with that statement. Human translation is a necessity!!! Especially in audiovisual translation, which involves techniques to synchronise the subtitles with the speech to provide the best viewer experience possible. From my experience of using AI in translation for both dubbing and subtitling, the technology would struggle to do things such as: ➡️ Break lines at logical points (like a full stop or a comma). ➡️ Localise properly (e.g. inch to meter). ➡️ Compress the text to match the duration of the speech. ➡️ Spell proper names correctly. ➡️ Translate humour and slang. So, AI still leaves us with a lot of rewriting and reviewing, which is time-consuming. These are just a few basic examples of how our work is not a luxury; it's essential. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise! We all need very good quality to keep well mentally and culturally. And we need to prioritise that. 💡 Any other reasons why human translation is a necessity? #litranslators ...more ...more

🎬 Why aren't all the spoken words included in the subtitles? Finding the sweet spot in subtitles: fitting the message without overwhelming the screen. My why... As I embarked on my journey as a freelance translator, it was important to think about why I wanted to do this. Someone asked me if I was sure this was the path I wanted to take or if I wanted to explore anything else. So, I sat and thought about what else I would do. And I can definitely come up with some ideas for other careers I could pursue, but none of them excite me like translation. I was lucky to have an amazing Spanish teacher in secondary school. I think she was key in igniting my love for languages, and that fascination has never gone away. Learning more about my native language and learning to master new ones is something I find endlessly interesting. The way we use words and their impact is so powerful. I am a language nerd through and through! And when you’re faced with a difficult sentence to translate, as frustrating as it can be sometimes, finding a solution that works is so rewarding. So, that’s why I do what I do. Because I love it, and I still get excited every time I learn something new ✨

publications.title: Project-Based and Self-Directed Learning
publications.subtitle: Third International Conference on Higher Education Advances, Editorial Universitat Politecnica de Valencia
publications.description: This article discusses the benefits of project-based and self-directed learning to develop competency in utilizing a second language and working collaboratively. The background premise of these modes of learning is provided, demonstrating that they work well for differentiated levels and language skills and improve student competence. Some of the areas examined are intercultural and scientific, ones that require the use of specific language in context. In addition, the concept of creating projects that increase student investment and motivation to make learning more relevant is juxtaposed with a student’s competency in an area after having participated in traditional approaches to learning. The overall benefit of the use of project-based and self-directed learning is that it allows the student to develop a higher skill set and greater engagement with the subject matter, producing better languageand content outcomes.

publications.description: The book offers a program for an English language curriculum that is specifically designed for the important and growing group of international medical professionals, with a focus on both instruction and assessment. International physicians in the United States now total more than 25% of the physician workforce.
